core.title: Review-ready only after full-profile proof
core.given: a governed acceptance-test-driven development (ATDD) task after behavioral GREEN and REFACTOR
core.when: you are about to declare the task complete or review-ready
core.then: Before you declare review-ready, rerun the behavioral proof, run the applicable active profiles, and correct every strict finding caused or exposed by the work.
prefer: Review-ready means the target behavior still passes and every active profile is green, with every strict finding cleared. Only this state counts as completion.
Follow the loop: RED -> smallest legal behavioral GREEN -> guided REFACTOR -> full-profile proof.
avoid: Using phase ordering to suppress a validator, weaken a threshold, or leave a security, architecture, runtime, traceability or other active constraint violated. Phase ordering never waives strict enforcement. Review-ready work MUST pass all active profiles.
Declaring completion at behavioral GREEN. It only proves the behavior exists.
core.why: Phase ordering never waives strict enforcement. GREEN and REFACTOR change the agent's response, not the validators, so completion requires the full-profile proof.
evidence: The behavioral proof was rerun before review and still passes.
The applicable active profiles were run and are all green. Every strict finding caused or exposed by the work is cleared.
verification: Review-ready is the point after behavioral GREEN and REFACTOR when the required behavior still passes and all active profiles are green. Only this state is completion.

Phase ordering never suppresses a validator, weakens a threshold, or permits a security, architecture, runtime, traceability or other active constraint to remain violated in review-ready work; phase is never a waiver of strict enforcement, and review-ready work must pass all active profiles.

No file-level detector of its own: the obligation is task-level, gated on task_has_acceptance and phase=review, and fires even with no new code change. The phase and active-profile-set facts need observers supplied by the realization.

fires: The agent is about to declare a governed task complete or review-ready, even if there is no new code change.
doesNotFire: Work with no behavioral acceptance under the governed ATDD loop.

neutralityNotes: The rule is a task-level phase-discipline obligation and names no stack mechanism: no command, path, file kind, suffix, lockfile, or detector/validator/finding id appears in bun.json, so no vocabulary key has a Bun value to bind and profileRequirements is empty (nothing missing, so proposedKeys is empty). The only stack-specific token is the profile-suite name 'ATDD Bun' ('Bun' names the runtime), replaced by 'the applicable active profiles' and recorded per item in bunOnly; instantiating the core with that name restores bun.json exactly. Which profiles are active is observed rather than assumed: the core keeps the 'active profile set' fact as needs_new_observer, and each realization supplies its own observer (e.g. reading the repository's profile configuration); the review phase likewise needs a phase observer. 'ATDD', 'review-ready', RED/GREEN/REFACTOR and the strict-finding disposition are methodology/enforcement concepts shared across stacks and stay in the core; the rule's term id review_ready is kept as a realization detail. The fires/doesNotFire strings in bun.json were already neutral and are kept verbatim.
